sentences.text:
Narashrit (Nirashrit) (Thakor) ... vs State Of Gujarat on 15 March,
2024
 
 R/Cr.Ma/4687/2024 Order

DATED: 15/03/2024  
 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR REGULAR BAIL - BEFORE  CHARGESHEET) NO. 4687 of 2024 ==========================================================
 NARASHRIT (NIRASHRIT) (THAKOR) SHAMLABHAI SUNDABHAI  (SHAMLABHAI CHUNDABHAI NIRASHRIT THAKOR)
 Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT ==========================================================
Appearance:
MITTAL N PATEL(7614) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 MR L B DABHI, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DIVYESH A. JOSHI  Date : 15/03/2024  ORAL ORDER 1.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned advocate Mr. Nimesh Patel submits that he has got instructions to appear for the original complainant.
He is permitted to file his Vakalatnama in the Registry.
Registry to accept the same.
2. Rule. Learned APP waives service of notice of Rule for and on behalf of respondent - State.

3. The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with C.R.No.11217029240044 of 2024 registered with Sami Police Station, District Patan, for the offence punishable under Sections 306, 498A and 114 of the Indian Penal Code.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4687/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/03/2024 undefined Narashrit (Nirashrit) (Thakor) ... vs State Of Gujarat on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14585933/
1 4. Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that considering the nature of the offence, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.
It is submitted that applicant is arrested on 31.01.2024 and since then he is in judicial custody.
It is submitted that the FIR has been filed by the father-in-law of the applicant accused.
It is alleged that the deceased - wife of the applicant has committed suicide on account of mental and physical torture given by the applicant accused.
Learned advocate submits that the marriage span is more than five years and general and vague allegations are levelled in the FIR.

It is further submitted that matter is amicably settled out of the Court and the complainant has also filed an affidavit inter alia stating that complainant has no objection if the applicant is enlarged on bail.
Thus, considering the aforesaid factual aspects, applicant may be enlarged on bail.
5. Learned APP appearing on behalf of the respondent-State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.
Learned APP submits that considering the gravity of offence, applicant may not be enlarged on bail.

6. Learned advocate Mr. Nimesh Patel appearing for the complainant has supported the submission of learned advocate for the applicant that the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4687/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/03/2024 undefined dispute is settled between the applicant accused and complainant outside the Court and therefore complainant has no objection if the applicant is enlarged on bail.
7.
Learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties do not press for further reasoned order.

8. I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers of the investigation and considered the allegations levelled against the applicant and the role played by the applicant.
It is found out from the record that applicant is in jail since 31.01.2024.
The investigation is already concluded and charge-sheet is filed.
The marriage span is more than 5 years.
It is also found out from the record that the allegations are general in nature.
Thus, considering the aforesaid factual aspects, I am inclined to consider this application.

9. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012]1 SCC 40 as well as in case of Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in (2022)10 SCC 51.
10.

entities.text: Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012]1 SCC 40
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in (2022)10 SCC 51
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the applicant in the FIR, without NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4687/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/03/2024 undefined discussing the evidence in detail, prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
11.
If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in the matter.
Bail bond to be executed before the lower Court having jurisdiction to try the case.
It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law.
13. At the trial, the trial Court shall not be influenced by the observations of preliminary nature qua the evidence at this stage made by this Court while enlarging the applicant on bail.
14. The present application stands allowed accordingly.
Rule is made absolute.
Direct service is permitted.
